weekNotes: Short batch by design: after the W32 cards, only two queue candidates carried a figure or topic not already shown last week — the rest restate the €9.90/€16.00 fares, the €11.90 airport total, the Sunday timetable or parking. Two cards, no padding.

Nothing on days 1–2: the W33 dates overlap the W32 tail — W32's tourist-tax and Torre del Mangia cards are dated Monday 10 and Tuesday 11 August. W33 starts Wednesday 12 August to avoid double-posting.

The day-trip budget card runs Friday 14 August so it lands ahead of weekend day-trippers. Sunday 16 August is a Palio date and the queue holds no Palio candidate — worth a targeted harvest before W34.

copy.caption:
Bus or train from Florence to Siena? On the current summer timetable the 131R bus takes about 75 minutes. The train usually takes 1 hour 20 to 1 hour 45, depending on whether it runs direct or changes at Empoli.

The bus is a road service, so traffic can add time — build in a margin. And the clock is only half the decision: the two arrive in very different parts of Siena.

copy.voiceover: Bus or train from Florence to Siena? On the current summer timetable, checked on the third of August, the one three one R bus takes about seventy-five minutes. The train usually takes longer — roughly one hour twenty to one hour forty-five, depending on whether it runs direct or changes at Empoli. The bus is a road service, so traffic can add time; build in a margin rather than planning to the minute. And the clock is only half the decision — the bus and the train arrive in very different parts of Siena. The full comparison, every number dated and checked, is at affittacameregliarchi dot com.

copy.caption:
Costing a Siena day trip from Florence? Return bus transport is €19.80 per person bought at the counter — €39.60 for two — before attraction tickets. No tourist tax, no room to pay for.

The catch day-trippers hit: some of Siena's best tickets are sold on the day only, in limited numbers, and they can be gone by the time you arrive.

copy.voiceover: Costing a day trip to Siena from Florence? By bus, return transport is nineteen euros eighty per person when you buy at the counter — thirty-nine euros sixty for two — as checked on the third of August. That is before attraction tickets, and it is the whole transport bill: a day trip pays no tourist tax and no room. The catch is timing. Some of Siena's best tickets are sold on the day only, in limited numbers, and they can be gone by the time a day-tripper arrives. The full costing, day trip against overnight, is at affittacameregliarchi dot com.
